args.sql:
WITH DynastyBudget AS (
    SELECT 
        a.artdynasty AS DynastyName,
        SUM(r.conservepriorityscore) AS TotalConservationPriorityIndex,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN c.maintbudgetstatus = 'Available' THEN 1 END) AS AdequateFundingCount,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN c.maintbudgetstatus != 'Available' THEN 1 END) AS InsufficientFundingCount,
        CASE 
            WHEN COUNT(CASE WHEN c.maintbudgetstatus = 'Available' THEN 1 END) < COUNT(CASE WHEN c.maintbudgetstatus != 'Available' THEN 1 END) 
            THEN 'Budget Crisis' 
            ELSE 'Within Budget' 
        END AS BudgetStatus
    FROM 
        artifactscore a
    JOIN 
        riskassessments r ON a.artregistry = r.artrefconcerned
    JOIN 
        conservationandmaintenance c ON a.artregistry = c.artrefmaintained
    GROUP BY 
        a.artdynasty
),
SummaryBudget AS (
    SELECT 
        'ALL DYNASTIES' AS DynastyName,
        SUM(TotalConservationPriorityIndex) AS TotalConservationPriorityIndex,
        SUM(AdequateFundingCount) AS AdequateFundingCount,
        SUM(InsufficientFundingCount) AS InsufficientFundingCount,
        CASE 
            WHEN SUM(AdequateFundingCount) < SUM(InsufficientFundingCount) 
            THEN 'Budget Crisis' 
            ELSE 'Within Budget' 
        END AS BudgetStatus
    FROM 
        DynastyBudget
)

SELECT * FROM DynastyBudget
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM SummaryBudget;

Database: museum
Task ID: museum_11

User Query:
I want to see which historical periods have adequate conservation resources and which might be facing a Budget Crisis. For each dynasty, show the dynasty name, their total conservation priority index, the count of artifacts with adequate funding, the count with insufficient funding, the budget efficiency value, and a budget status that indicates 'Budget Crisis' if the dynasty meets the defined issue criteria, and 'Within Budget' otherwise. Besides, please include a summary row for all dynasties combined labeled as 'ALL DYNASTIES'.

You have a budget of 16.0 bird-coins. Use your tools to explore the database, clarify ambiguities with the user, and submit your final SQL efficiently.
